reconcile.connective: JFB flatly denies any textual ground for identifying Luke's unnamed sinner with a named woman, keeping her distinct from John's Mary of Bethany.

discrepancy.connective: D. F. Strauss noted Luke and John describe the distinctive foot-drying-with-hair detail 'in nearly the same words,' concluding this is one story, not two.

skeptic.name: David Friedrich Strauss
skeptic.work: The Life of Jesus Critically Examined
skeptic.attribution: David Friedrich Strauss (1808-1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (German orig. Das Leben Jesu, 1835-36; Eng. trans. 1846), Part II, § 89.

excerpts.excerpt_text: There is no ground whatever for the popular notion that this woman was Mary Magdalene, nor do we know what her name was.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB directly denies the popular identification linking Luke's unnamed sinner to a named Gospel woman, the harmonizing move that keeps her distinct from John's Mary of Bethany.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley lists this exact pairing under events distinguished by occurring at different times: "Christ anointed at one time, Matt. xxvi. 7; John xii. 3; at another time, Luke vii. 37, 38 (the best critics hold that the anointing in the first two passages was quite distinct from that mentioned by Luke)," p. 411.

link.title: GotQuestions: What is the significance of Jesus being anointed by a woman with expensive perfume?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment distinguishing the Luke 7 sinner from John 12's Mary of Bethany as separate anointings.
